criteria.descriptor: Every identified mechanism and fix is technically correct: the post-outcome feature is excluded on prediction-time availability grounds; target encoding must be out-of-fold; preprocessing must fit per fold; grouping is on borrower_id; the split must be time-ordered. Full marks require no false claims (e.g., that regularization, more data, or a random holdout would fix leakage, or that target encoding 'on training data only' is inherently safe).

Covers all five distinct leakage sources present (post-outcome feature, full-data target encoding, full-data preprocessing, repeat-borrower group leakage, temporal leakage) plus an end-to-end corrected validation and at least one verification method. Score scales with how many distinct, correct sources and remedies are found; missing the higher-impact ones (post-outcome feature, temporal, group) costs more than missing the scaler-in-pipeline point.

Explains the causal mechanism by which each source specifically inflates CV — leaking the label, future information, or validation-fold statistics — and justifies why the proposed split mirrors the production train/predict boundary, rather than merely listing fixes by name.

Well-organized, cleanly separates diagnosis from remediation, and uses precise terminology (out-of-fold encoding, point-in-time/as-of correctness, GroupKFold, TimeSeriesSplit, out-of-time holdout, adversarial validation) correctly and economically.

expected_answer_points: Identifies num_collections_calls as post-outcome/target-proxy leakage — its value only exists after default and is unavailable at scoring time — and fixes it via point-in-time feature availability (drop post-decision features).

Identifies the full-dataset mean/target encoding of employer_name as target leakage (each row's encoding uses its own label), and fixes it with out-of-fold/nested encoding fit only on training folds, with smoothing for rare categories.

Identifies imputation medians and StandardScaler fit on the full dataset as train/validation contamination, and fixes it by putting all preprocessing in an sklearn Pipeline so it fits per fold on training data only.
Identifies group leakage from repeat borrowers under KFold(shuffle=True) and fixes it with GroupKFold/StratifiedGroupKFold keyed on borrower_id.

Identifies temporal leakage from random shuffling (training on the future to predict the past) versus production's train-past/predict-future, and fixes it with a time-ordered split or out-of-time holdout.

Proposes an integrated corrected validation that mirrors production: point-in-time features, pipeline-inside-CV, and a time-ordered, group-aware split with an out-of-time holdout as the production proxy.
Describes at least one detection/verification method (feature-ablation, importance audit, adversarial validation, or comparing corrected CV to an out-of-time holdout) to confirm leakage is removed.
common_pitfalls: Attributing the gap to ordinary overfitting or model complexity and recommending regularization / hyperparameter tuning instead of fixing the leaked features and validation design.
Treating the target encoding as safe because it is 'on training data,' missing that it must be computed out-of-fold or it leaks each row's own label.
Fixing only the textbook scaler/imputer-in-pipeline issue and overlooking the higher-impact post-outcome feature (num_collections_calls), the temporal split, and the repeat-borrower group leakage.

Recommending StratifiedKFold or a random train/test holdout as the remedy, not realizing the same leakage contaminates a random holdout and that group and temporal structure must be respected instead.
Failing to recognize num_collections_calls as a consequence of the label — treating it as a legitimate predictor — and so never enforcing point-in-time feature availability.
Confusing data leakage with covariate/distribution shift, or proposing to 'collect more data' rather than removing the label/future information from features and folds.
reference_answer:
The 0.96 CV score is an artifact of at least five distinct leakage mechanisms; production (~0.71) is the honest number.

1) Post-outcome / target-proxy feature. `num_collections_calls` is generated *after* a loan becomes delinquent — it is a downstream consequence of the label, not a predictor available at application time. At scoring time for a new application it is unknown (usually 0), so the model has learned a near-deterministic shortcut. Fix: enforce point-in-time (as-of) feature availability — every feature must be knowable at the prediction cutoff (application time); drop `num_collections_calls` and any other post-decision field.

2) Target (mean) encoding over the full dataset. Encoding `employer_name` with the default rate leaks the label directly into a feature: each row's encoded value is computed using its own label (and the validation rows' labels). With high cardinality (employer near one-to-one with borrower) this approaches memorizing the target. Fix: compute the encoding out-of-fold / nested inside CV, fit only on the training partition, with smoothing/regularization for rare employers.

3) Preprocessing fit on the full dataset. Imputation medians and scaler statistics include the validation rows, leaking distributional information. Fix: wrap impute → scale → encode in an sklearn `Pipeline` and pass the Pipeline to `cross_val_score`, so each fold fits preprocessing on its training split only.

4) Group leakage. `KFold(shuffle=True)` scatters a repeat borrower's applications across train and validation, letting the model memorize borrower-specific risk. Fix: `GroupKFold`/`StratifiedGroupKFold` keyed on `borrower_id` so a borrower never spans folds.

5) Temporal leakage. Random shuffling trains on 2023 to predict 2020, whereas production always predicts the future. Fix: a time-ordered split — `TimeSeriesSplit` / forward-chaining, or a hard out-of-time holdout (train ≤2022, validate 2023) — and keep borrower groups from crossing the temporal boundary.

Corrected setup: a point-in-time feature table with an application-time cutoff; all preprocessing/encoding inside a Pipeline that fits per fold; a time-ordered, group-aware split; final estimate on an out-of-time holdout as the production proxy.

Verification: ablate suspicious features and watch CV collapse toward 0.71; audit feature importances for a single dominating feature; run adversarial validation (train-vs-production classifier) to detect distribution shift; and confirm the corrected CV estimate ≈ out-of-time holdout ≈ production.
